title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Appendix D: Being Moral in the Brave New World
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
primary_topics: Appendix D: Fr. Ranhilio Callangan Aquino on the ethics of human cloning, genetic engineering, and embryo manipulation
sub_topics: The moral status of the human embryo
Constitutional recognition of the sanctity of family life (Art. II, Sec. 12)
Ethical considerations of cloning and genetic engineering
Being moral in a 'brave new world' of biotechnology

people: Ranhilio Callangan Aquino (Fr.; Philippine Judicial Academy)

stances.claim: The moral status of the embryo and the ethics of cloning and genetic engineering demand serious philosophical and constitutional reflection.

notable_anecdotes: He opens by asking whether a human embryo is merely 'a clump of cells.'
one_paragraph_summary: Appendix D reproduces Fr. Ranhilio Callangan Aquino's essay on the ethics of the 'brave new world' of human cloning and genetic engineering. He probes the moral status of the human embryo, invokes the Constitution's recognition of the sanctity of family life (Art. II, Sec. 12), and calls for serious philosophical reflection on manipulating human life.
